skill.name: azure-mgmt-fabric-dotnet
skill.description: Guides .NET developers through Azure.ResourceManager.Fabric management-plane operations for Microsoft Fabric capacities, including provisioning, scaling, suspension, resume, deletion, SKU lookup, and name availability checks.
skill.summary: Build .NET management workflows for Microsoft Fabric capacity resources through Azure Resource Manager.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline SDK names, fixed package install examples, placeholder Azure credential names, and official reference links. The review found no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden execution intent. A semantic medium finding remains because the Azure management workflows can affect billing and availability.

remediation.issue: Cost and availability impact from capacity lifecycle operations
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before create, update, suspend, resume, or delete actions. Echo subscription, resource group, capacity name, region, and SKU first.

remediation.issue: Credential placeholders may be copied into prompts or logs
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to configure secrets outside chat, prefer managed identity or secret stores, and never paste AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET values.

remediation.issue: Examples use placeholder names and admin identities
remediation.suggestion: Ask users to replace placeholders with approved tenant values and verify RBAC before running generated code.

semantic_findings.title: Privileged Azure Capacity Operations
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents workflows that create, scale, suspend, resume, and delete Microsoft Fabric capacities. These are legitimate actions, but they can affect cost and service availability without clear confirmation.

content.value_statement: Managing Microsoft Fabric capacity through ARM can require many SDK calls and state checks. This skill provides focused .NET guidance for provisioning, scaling, suspension, resume, deletion, SKU lookup, and safe authentication.
actual_capabilities: Shows package setup and DefaultAzureCredential authentication for Azure.ResourceManager.Fabric.
Provides .NET examples for creating, reading, updating, suspending, resuming, and deleting Fabric capacities.
Demonstrates capacity listing at resource group and subscription scope.
Explains name availability checks and SKU enumeration for location planning.
Summarizes key SDK types, SKU sizes, states, best practices, and ARM error handling.
limitations: Covers the ARM management plane only, not Fabric workspace, lakehouse, or warehouse data APIs.
Requires an Azure subscription, suitable RBAC permissions, resource groups, and identity configuration.
Does not verify live SDK versions, regional SKU availability, or tenant policy changes.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted before production use.

use_cases.title: Automate Capacity Lifecycle
use_cases.description: Platform engineers can build .NET services that create, scale, suspend, resume, and delete Fabric capacities.

use_cases.title: Control Analytics Costs
use_cases.description: Fabric administrators can plan SKU changes and suspend idle capacity with clearer state checks.

use_cases.title: Build Internal Tools
use_cases.description: Application developers can add name availability, SKU lookup, and capacity status workflows to internal portals.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to install Azure.ResourceManager.Fabric and authenticate with DefaultAzureCredential for a local .NET project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Capacity
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a .NET workflow to create a Microsoft Fabric capacity named [name] in [region] with SKU [sku] and admins [admins].

prompt_templates.title: Manage Capacity State
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me update a Fabric capacity SKU, then suspend or resume it only after checking the current provisioning state.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production-safe capacity management service with confirmation steps, RBAC assumptions, retry handling, logging boundaries, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Create a new F64 capacity for a development resource group.
output: Lists required subscription, resource group, region, SKU, and administrator inputs.
Describes the create operation, wait behavior, state checks, and expected failure cases.
Flags cost impact and asks for confirmation before execution.

output_examples.input: Find whether a capacity name is available and which SKUs can run in West US 2.
output_examples.output: The response outlines name checks, SKU enumeration, regional constraints, and a decision summary for the requested region.

output_examples.input: Suspend an idle production capacity safely.
output: Verifies the target capacity, current state, and business impact.
Recommends approval, maintenance timing, and post-operation validation before suspension.

best_practices: Confirm subscription, resource group, location, SKU, and capacity name before any change.
Use DefaultAzureCredential and RBAC, and never paste secret values into prompts.
Use completed waits, state checks, and RequestFailedException handling for long-running operations.
anti_patterns: Deleting or suspending production capacities without explicit approval.
Hardcoding credentials, tenant secrets, or administrator identifiers in reusable code.
Using this management SDK for workspace, lakehouse, warehouse, or item-level data tasks.

faq.question: What does this skill help manage?
faq.answer: It helps manage Microsoft Fabric capacity resources through Azure Resource Manager using .NET.

faq.question: Does it cover Fabric workspaces and lakehouses?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on capacity management and not Fabric data-plane resources.

faq.question: Which authentication pattern does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends DefaultAzureCredential with properly configured Azure identity and RBAC permissions.

faq.question: Can it help control Fabric capacity cost?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains SKU changes and suspension workflows that can reduce idle compute cost.

faq.question: Should production changes be automatic?
faq.answer: No. Production create, update, suspend, resume, and delete actions should require explicit approval.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
